subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which model-visible tool-result policy should OpenClaw use for DeepSeek cache mitigation: narrow heartbeat/status summaries, opt-in compaction middleware, or broad provider-level hiding?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not syntax; it is whether hiding classes of tool results from the next model turn is an acceptable product/runtime policy for existing agents.

options.title: Narrow and rebase
options.body: Limit summaries to maintainer-approved low-information status outputs, retarget the package-level provider converters, and require live DeepSeek proof.

options.title: Prefer opt-in compaction
options.body: Keep provider replay faithful by default and route high-volume exec/bash compaction through Tokenjuice or a similar explicit tool-result middleware.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Leave this PR paused or close it later if maintainers choose a different fix path for the canonical tool-output cache issue.

recommendation.title: Narrow and rebase
recommendation.body: Limit summaries to maintainer-approved low-information status outputs, retarget the package-level provider converters, and require live DeepSeek proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-main history signal on the package-level provider and tool-result replay code this PR must now target.
